(rules, not AI — a fact never invented by the model)
calls Claude, validates the JSON reply,
Every field returned is stored — nothing is discarded.
Feeds the Eval Log & override rate.
Schema present, not exercised in this POC
Migrations create all six tables named in the
brief so the schema matches it. Processes 1
and 2 are not built for this demo — a scope
Sanctions screening is out of scope too:
the brief names it but Appendix A supplies
How a vendor gets screened — numbers match the badges above
Analyst signs in and opens the Vendor Onboarding form.
Form is posted to the backend; fields and formats are validated.
Screening Engine queries the vendors table: exact ABN match, exact bank match, partial match.
Those rule findings, plus the form, are handed to the LLM Gateway.
Gateway calls Claude with a system + user prompt from /prompts/.
Claude’s JSON reply (tier, anomalies, checklist, rationale) is validated and written to the vendor row.
Reviewer sees the result and can approve it or override the tier — the override posts back through the same channel as step 2.
Audit Logger writes that decision, and any override, to audit_log — nothing self-approves.
Dashed arrow = reading data back to a screen, not a new write.
If Claude times out or returns bad JSON: one retry, then the screen shows the rule findings alone with a plain banner —
it never blanks and it never auto-approves.
Not built, by design: sanctions screening (no watchlist supplied), Processes 1 & 2, SSO, mobile layouts, CI/CD, async queue.
FinanceOS technical assessment · Process 3 · Vendor Risk & Onboarding Screener · seed data: 25 vendors, 3 exact duplicates, 2 partial duplicates
